screening_results.reason: The study is excluded because it does not meet Inclusion Criterion I7: the regulated stimuli are not static visual images. Participants listened to audio vignettes and spoken negative self-belief (NSB) statements (auditory stimuli) rather than viewing static pictures, so the study does not address the review’s stimulus modality requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I6 (reappraisal used as a regulation strategy), I8 (contains a healthy control group). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (stimuli are static visual images). Note: the paper appears to report whole-brain task contrasts and group analyses (and likely reports coordinates in figures/supplement), but failure to meet I7 is sufficient for exclusion. No exclusion criteria from the review (E4–E8) were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that implements distancing, a form of reappraisal, to down-regulate emotion (I6). Emotional stimuli are static IAPS pictures (I7). The sample is healthy adults with exclusions for psychiatric/neurological conditions and a separate healthy control sample reported (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., DISTANCING > negative-VIEW; I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster reports and MNI coordinates in tables (I10), and whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables (I11). Full text includes methods, results, and tables with coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met. Given these points, include the study for the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using instructed cognitive reappraisal-like strategies (increase/decrease via causal attributions) with static face photographs and reports within-task regulation contrasts ([increase+decrease] > view) using whole-brain voxelwise analysis. However, the sample includes a clinical group (MDD) and healthy controls but the paper reports regulation results primarily at the combined/group-level (and ROI-masked overlap analyses) rather than providing a standalone, whole-brain group-level reappraise>view (or equivalent) contrast with peak coordinates for the healthy control group alone. Because the meta-analysis requires whole-brain coordinates specifically for the healthy adult control group (I8), this study does not meet that inclusion criterion and cannot contribute healthy-group whole-brain coordinates for reappraisal. Hence EXCLUDED.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with healthy trauma-exposed control participants and reports within-task regulation contrasts and whole-brain peak coordinates, the emotion regulation strategy tested is distraction (working-memory load during presentation of negative IAPS images), not reappraisal or its broadly defined variants (reinterpretation, perspective-taking, distancing). The review’s I6 specifically requires reappraisal (or its accepted equivalents). Therefore the study fails to meet I6 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of reappraisal using static IAPS images in healthy adults (meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9), the neuroimaging analyses are reported using a predetermined ROI approach only. The manuscript does not report group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or peak coordinates in a standard space for the reappraisal contrasts; results are presented as ROI statistics/tables. Therefore it fails I10 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only results without an accompanying whole-brain map). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly implements cognitive reappraisal as an emotion regulation strategy using static visual images (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., [view NEG – reappraise]) at the group level and notes complementary whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates provided in the supplementary material. Although primary ROI/SVC results are emphasized, the authors affirm whole-brain voxelwise results in the supplement, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain coordinates. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, patient-only samples) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (supplementary tables referenced but absence of supplemental files is acceptable). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11.

This study is excluded because it does not include a healthy adult group reported separately (I8 not met) and it uses an ROI-based analytic approach rather than reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation peaks/coordinates (meets exclusion criterion E5). Satisfied inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal as regulation strategy), I7 (static visual images/IAPS), and I9 (within-task contrast ReappNeg > LookNeg reported). Not satisfied: I8 (no healthy control group reported), I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise peak coordinates reported; analyses relied on ROI beta weights and PCA), therefore the study does not provide the required whole-brain coordinates. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly implements cognitive reappraisal (distancing) as the regulation strategy (Decrease condition) in response to static visual IAPS images. Participants were healthy adult volunteers. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Decrease > Look-Negative; Decrease > Look-Neutral) and describes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses thresholded at P<0.05 FWE with coordinates referenced to MNI space. Reporting of whole-brain results and coordinates (tables/figures/supplement) is indicated. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, patient-only without separate healthy group, or disallowed perspective-taking) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an explicit reappraisal paradigm (reappraise > negative view) with static visual images drawn from the IAPS. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=35) alongside a patient group; the paper reports within-task (reappraise > negative view and negative view > neutral view) group-level whole-brain analyses with cluster results and peak coordinates (main results and Appendix tables referenced). The methods describe voxelwise whole-brain statistics (FWE-corrected and cluster-wise corrections) and report anatomical MNI labeling, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only reporting, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, supplementary table references). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal paradigm (Regulate vs Maintain) with static visual images (neutral and negative pictures). The sample includes a healthy-weight control group with separate reported within-group and between-group task results. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and peak MNI coordinates are reported (e.g., vmPFC x=-10,y=64,z=-18; extrastriate x=56,y=-72,z=10). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation, whole-brain analyses with cluster-level correction, and provides sufficient methodological and result detail. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used as ER strategy), I8 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with peak coordinates reported), I11 (coordinates/tables reported). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I7 — Stimuli are participant-generated autobiographical narratives and negative self-belief sentences (text), not static visual images (e.g., IAPS pictures, photographs). Therefore the study does not meet the stimulus-type requirement and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a reappraisal (distancing) SUPPRESS condition and IAPS static images, and it includes a healthy control group with within-task contrasts (MAINTAIN vs SUPPRESS). However, all reported results are ROI-based network/connectivity (NBS, graph theory) analyses rather than voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked activation maps with peak coordinates in a standard space. Therefore it does not provide the required whole-brain voxelwise coordinates. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI/connectivity-based results without a whole-brain map) and E6 (connectivity-only analyses without accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I10 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map with peak coordinates reported); I11 (not applicable because coordinates/maps are not provided in text/tables). Consequently the study must be excluded from the coordinates-based reappraisal meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that used explicit reappraisal instructions with static visual images and included a healthy control group; first-level and group-level reappraisal contrasts (reappraise > attend) were computed and whole-brain FWE-corrected analyses are reported. However, the provided full text does not include peak coordinates or coordinate tables/figures for the reported whole-brain results (placeholders like “see and” suggest missing figures/tables). Inclusion criterion I10 (reporting peak coordinates in standard space) cannot be verified from the supplied text. Because I10 is not confirmed and coordinates appear absent from this full text, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis dataset unless full coordinates can be provided. Full text appears incomplete for the purposes of coordinate extraction (missing tables/figures).

This study should be excluded because it does not include (and does not report separately) a healthy adult control group. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal as regulation strategy), I7 (static visual images/IAPS), I9 (within-task contrast Reappraise > Look-Negative), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with peak MNI coordinates reported), I11 (results/tables clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (no healthy adult sample or separate HC results reported). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that implements an explicit reappraisal instruction (reappraise > attend) to down-regulate emotion (methods: reappraisal task described), using static visual images (IAPS and alcohol photographs). The sample includes a healthy control group (n=39) reported alongside patient group, and first-level and second-level within-task contrasts for reappraisal (reappraise > attend) per emotion were computed and analyzed. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (results described as whole-brain FWE-corrected, and tables/figures with peak coordinates are referenced for group effects), meeting the requirement for peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 (and I11). No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the report used an ROI-based analysis with small-volume correction and does not present an accompanying whole-brain, voxelwise group-level statistical map with peak coordinates for the regulation contrast in the healthy control group. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (cognitive reappraisal used for down-regulation), I7 (stimuli were static visual images), I8 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts computed: fear regulate > attend and OCD regulate > attend). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I10 (no clear whole-brain group-level task-evoked map with reported peak coordinates in standard space for the regulation contrast in healthy controls). The full text appears complete; supplemental materials are referenced but whole-brain coordinate tables are not provided in the main text excerpt, and the authors emphasize ROI/SVC results, so the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain coordinates.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adults viewing static negative faces and uses whole-brain data (I5, I7, I8 satisfied), it does not implement an explicit reappraisal manipulation nor report a within-task reappraisal contrast. The task was a face-versus-shape matching task with no instructions to reappraise; reappraisal is inferred post hoc via pattern correspondence rather than being used as the regulated strategy in the task (I6 not met). The paper does not report a within-task regulation contrast (e.g., “reappraise > look”) for the target sample (I9 not met), nor does it provide group-level whole-brain activation coordinates for a reappraisal condition emerging from the task (I10 not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using reappraisal to down-regulate responses to static IAPS images and includes a healthy control group with within-task contrast reappraise > attend-negative, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates for whole-brain group-level results in a standard space (MNI/Talairach). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal as ER strategy), I7 (static visual images), I8 (healthy control group reported separately), I9 (within-task contrast reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no peak coordinates in standard reference space reported in the provided full text or supplements). No exclusion criteria from the review were clearly triggered by the provided text. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis based on failure to meet I10.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed participants to reappraise unpleasant IAPS pictures (reinterpretation) and reports the reappraise > maintain contrast. Stimuli are static visual images (IAPS). The sample includes a healthy low-risk adult group (results reported separately in group comparisons) and within-task, group-level whole-brain analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures referenced). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (meets I5 and I8) but does NOT meet critical review inclusion criteria: the emotional stimuli were film/video clips (movie clips) rather than static visual images (violates I7); the task was a non-directive emotion-eliciting viewing with no instruction to reappraise or otherwise regulate emotion (violates I6); the study does not report any within-task reappraisal/regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) (violates I9); and the provided text does not present peak whole-brain activation coordinates in a standard space for a reappraisal-related contrast (I10 not satisfied/unclear). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults who performed cognitive reappraisal (self-focused distancing) to down-regulate emotion elicited by static IAPS pictures. The manuscript reports within-task contrasts for regulation (Decrease > LookNeg) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space (tables/figures described). The sample consists of healthy adult participants and analyses include whole-brain results as well as ROI follow-ups. The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of explicit emotion regulation that used reappraisal (and response modulation) as instructed strategies, applied to static IAPS images in a healthy adult sample (n=24) with no reported psychiatric/neurological disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., regulate > maintain; direction-specific contrasts) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (amygdala and dorsomedial PFC coordinates reported). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This article meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that implements an explicit reappraisal emotion regulation task (Reappraise vs Maintain; I6). The regulated stimuli are static visual images (IAPS scenes) and facial photographs (I7). The sample comprises healthy adults with no reported neurological or psychiatric disorders (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Reappraise > Maintain) (I9) and describes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction; peak coordinates are reported for multiple clusters (e.g., amygdala coordinates and PPI peak coordinates), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, standard-space peak coordinates (I10). Whole-brain results are presented/described in text and figures/tables (I11). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it includes a task-based fMRI experiment (Experiment 3) using cognitive reappraisal instructions (Increase/Maintain/Decrease) to regulate emotion elicited by static IAPS images, with healthy adult participants, within-task contrasts reported (e.g., Increase vs Maintain, Decrease vs Maintain), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak MNI coordinates and thresholding reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not an ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly implemented cognitive reappraisal (reappraising > attending-negative contrasts) during scanning using static visual images from the IAPS. The sample includes a healthy control group reported separately (HC n=14) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (GLM one-sample and group comparisons with peak coordinates/tables referenced, e.g., Tables S1–S4). The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of reappraisal in healthy adults using static visual images and reports the ReappNeg vs LookNeg contrast (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied), the paper presents analyses based on ROI beta-weights (AAL ROIs) and PCA/discriminant analysis and does not report group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation peak coordinates in a standard space. No tables or peak coordinates for whole-brain contrasts are provided in the full text, so the study violates exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI analyses without an accompanying whole-brain map). Therefore it cannot be included for a coordinate-based meta-analysis that requires whole-brain reported peaks (I10 not met).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) it is a task-based fMRI study; (I6) includes an explicit cognitive reappraisal condition (Reappraise) used to down-regulate negative affect; (I7) the regulated stimuli are static visual images (IAPS); (I8) sample comprises healthy adults with screening for psychiatric disorders and results reported for that group; (I9) reports the within-task contrast Reappraise > Look-Negative; (I10) provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (FWE-corrected clusters); (I11) coordinates and results are presented in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly uses self-focused reappraisal to increase and decrease emotional responses to static visual stimuli (angry and neutral faces). The sample includes a healthy control group reported separately (n=22). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., increase > view-angry, decrease > view-angry, increase > decrease) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with tables/figures (thresholded maps and coordinate tables) in standard space. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of emotional face viewing in healthy adults (unaffected first-degree relatives and controls) using static visual stimuli and reports group-level activation coordinates, but it does not implement or test an in-scanner reappraisal/regulation task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual image stimuli - faces), I8 (healthy adult sample reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reappraisal instruction/manipulation during the fMRI task; emotion regulation was measured only via self-report ERQ), I9 (no within-task regulation contrasts such as reappraise>look), I10 (analyses are ROI-focused and between-group contrasts rather than a reported whole-brain voxelwise regulation contrast). Exclusion criteria triggered: E5 (study used an ROI approach without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map for a reappraisal contrast) and E7 (results focus on between-group contrasts and do not report the required within-task reappraisal contrasts for healthy controls). Therefore the study does not meet the review’s requirement of an in-scanner reappraisal regulation contrast and is excluded.

No exclusion criteria from E4–E8 apply. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal/distancing used as regulation), I7 (static visual images: IAPS/Emopics), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), and I10 (whole-brain analyses performed and referenced). Inclusion criterion not met: I8 (target sample = healthy adults). The HC group is mixed-age (12.1–29.5 years), including minors/adolescents; the study does not provide an adult-only healthy sample that can be isolated for analysis. Because the meta-analysis objective requires healthy adult participants, this study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (supplementary materials referenced but acceptable).

This is a well-documented task-based fMRI study that includes a reappraisal condition using static IAPS images and reports whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > attend negative) and peak coordinates for group-level analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used), I7 (static visual stimuli), I9 (within-task reappraisal contrasts defined), and I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with reported peak coordinates). However, the study sample is primarily clinical (schizophrenia) with a healthy control (HC) group included; the full text provided does not report group-level, whole-brain reappraisal contrast results for the healthy control group separately (results/coordinates for HC-only are not presented in the main text; main task effects and group differences are referred to as being in Supplementary Materials). Because the meta-analysis requires that, for patient studies, healthy control results be reported separately (I8), and that target healthy-adult maps/coordinates be available, I8 is not satisfied based on the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are directly triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for the review due to lack of separately reported healthy-adult whole-brain reappraisal results.

The study was excluded because it does not include a group of healthy adult participants completing the reappraisal task with separable results (violates I8). Although the paper is a task-based fMRI study using reappraisal (I5, I6) with static visual images (I7), reports within-task reappraisal contrasts (I9), and presents voxel-wise whole-brain analyses with coordinate tables referenced in the supplement (I10), the reported task results are for a PTSD patient sample (clinical population). The only healthy cohort (N=14) underwent TMS-fMRI mapping, not the reappraisal task, so no healthy adult whole-brain reappraisal activation map is provided. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) were triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (decrease) to regulate emotion to static IAPS images. The paper reports within-task reappraisal contrasts (decrease-negative > look-negative) and performs whole-brain group-level analyses with corrected maps and tables of peak coordinates (see Table 3 and whole-brain results). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using cognitive reappraisal (situation-focused reinterpretation) to up- and down-regulate emotion (I5,I6). Stimuli are static visual images (IAPS and internet photos) presented during regulation (I7). Sample includes a healthy adult group reported separately (27 healthy females) (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., down-regulation vs look, up-regulation vs look, reappraise vs distraction) (I9). Group-level whole-brain analyses are described (exploratory whole-brain results) and peak coordinates are reported in the text/tables (MNI coordinates for vmPFC, dlPFC, vlPFC, etc.), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not empathy-without-regulation). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. Study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adult participants using an affect-labeling (AL) task with static facial images, reporting group-level whole-brain peaks and contrasts (AL > gender label). However it does not use reappraisal (reinterpretation, explicit perspective-taking, or distancing) as the emotion regulation strategy required by inclusion criterion I6: the task is affect labeling (an incidental/implicit labeling procedure), not reappraisal. Therefore I6 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (static visual image stimuli), I8 (healthy adult sample), I9 (within-task emotion-regulation contrast AL>GL), I10 (group-level whole-brain peaks/coordinates reported), I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Exclusion therefore based on failure to meet I6 (reappraisal).

All inclusion criteria are satisfied: this is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that implemented explicit cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise condition) as the regulation strategy (I6) using static visual images from the IAPS (I7). The sample includes a healthy control group and the paper reports group-specific results and within-group analyses for HCs (I8). The authors report within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Reappraise > Look-Neutral) (I9). Analyses are whole-brain voxelwise with cluster correction and peak coordinates in MNI space are provided (I10). Results are presented in figures/tables described in the text (I11). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is available and complete. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply.

This paper is a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (distancing) with static IAPS images and includes a healthy control group. However, the full text presents only between-group whole-brain contrasts (marijuana users > controls) and does not report a group-level, whole-brain reappraisal contrast (e.g., reappraise>look) for the healthy control group alone. The review’s target requires a group-level whole-brain task activation map with peak coordinates for the healthy adult sample (or a separable healthy control within-task contrast). Because only between-group contrasts are reported, exclusion criterion E7 applies and inclusion criteria I9 and I10 (within-task group contrast and corresponding whole-brain peak coordinates for the target healthy sample) are not met, so the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a reappraisal (distancing) strategy to regulate emotions elicited by static visual images (IAPS and photographs). The sample comprises healthy participants aged 6–23 (includes healthy adults). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Reappraisal/Negative > Reactivity/Negative) and group-level whole-brain analyses with peak MNI coordinates reported in tables and text. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that used reappraisal on static visual images and reports whole-brain group-level activation coordinates (Reappraise > Maintain). However, the sample consists entirely of clinical patients with anxiety and/or depression and no healthy control group or separately reported healthy-adult results are provided. Inclusion criterion I8 (at least one group of healthy adults) is therefore not met, so the study must be excluded. Included criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal as the regulation strategy), I7 (static visual images/IAPS), I9 (within-task Reappraise>Maintain contrast), I10 (whole-brain coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive reappraisal using static visual images (IAPS/EPS) and reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look-negative) and whole-brain group-level results with coordinates (e.g., right amygdala peak [18,0,-20]). However, the target-sample criterion (I8) requires at least one group of healthy adults reported separately. The healthy control group here is a mixed ‘youth’ sample aged 15–25 years (includes minors/adolescents) and the paper does not report a separate healthy adult-only group or analyses restricted to adults. Therefore it does not meet I8 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this review. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none of E4–E8 apply. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (contains a healthy adult non-offender control group), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation: distraction vs engagement). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (regulation strategy is distraction/engagement of audiotaped narratives, not reappraisal/distancing/reinterpretation as defined), I7 (stimuli are audiotaped narrative scripts, not static visual images), I10 (provided full text does not report peak coordinates in standard space for whole-brain maps within the supplied content). Because it fails I6 and I7 (and I10 is not verifiable in the provided full text), the study does not match the review objective and is excluded.

Study 2 is a task-based fMRI investigation that implemented cognitive reappraisal instructions (“regulate” condition) to down-regulate emotion elicited by static visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (regulate > experience) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with peak coordinates reported in MNI space (e.g., left lateral frontal peak x = -60, y = 20, z = 32) and additional coordinate tables referenced in the Supporting Information. A healthy control group is included and results for controls are reported separately (within-participant analyses and group maps). The full text contains Introduction, Methods (task, imaging, analyses), Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal using static IAPS images in healthy adult participants (I5, I6, I7, I8 satisfied) and peak coordinates are reported for group contrasts (I10), the reported neuroimaging results in the provided full text appear to consist primarily of between-group comparisons (high-Mach vs low-Mach) derived from the IAPS2–IAPS1 reappraisal contrast. The article does not present a clear, group-level within-task whole-brain contrast of reappraisal versus baseline/maintain for the healthy sample as a whole (e.g., “reappraise > look”) in the main text (the within-task activation map is only alluded to as shown in supplementary material). Because the manuscript reports mainly between-group contrasts and does not clearly provide a within-task group-level whole-brain regulation contrast for the target sample, it meets exclusion criterion E7 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions). Inclusion criterion I9 (reporting at least one within-task regulation contrast for the target sample) is not clearly met.

Exclusion E5 applies: the study reports ROI-based analyses (AAL anatomical ROI beta weights) and explicitly notes no conclusions can be made at the whole-brain level; no whole-brain voxelwise maps or peak coordinates in standard space are presented. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (explicit reappraisal task used), I7 (static visual images—IAPS pictures), I9 (within-task contrast reported: Reappraise > Maintain). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 (target sample: no healthy adult group reported separately—sample is clinical SAD patients only), I10 (whole-brain evidence with peak coordinates reported is not provided). Because the review requires healthy control whole-brain activation coordinates for reappraisal, this study must be excluded.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that implements an implicit form of cognitive reappraisal (preceding neutral/positive vs negative descriptions — reinterpretation/incidental reappraisal; I6). The regulated stimuli are static visual images from the IAPS (I7). Participants are healthy adults screened for psychiatric/neurological disorders (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (NNEG-DESC vs NEG-DESC; I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with corrected thresholds and peak coordinates (Talairach/MNI) presented in tables/figures (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

Excluded because the study does not implement reappraisal as defined in inclusion criterion I6. The task’s appraisal condition (like/dislike) is an emotion labeling/self-appraisal manipulation without instruction to reinterpret, distance, or explicitly up-/down-regulate emotional responses; therefore it does not meet I6. The full text is complete and the study does satisfy several other inclusion criteria (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10): it is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using static visual images, reports within-task contrasts (like/dislike > male/female) and provides whole-brain peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are met. Because the meta-analysis specifically targets reappraisal paradigms (reinterpretation/perspective-taking/distancing) and this study’s appraisal/labeling manipulation lacks an explicit reappraisal/regulation instruction, it must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using reappraisal of static visual images (I5, I6, I7, I8 satisfied) and it reports within-task contrasts related to reappraisal (reappraise vs watch) implemented as PPI/gPPI contrasts (I9 satisfied). This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly used cognitive reappraisal (reinterpretation/distancing) to down-regulate negative emotions elicited by static visual images (IAPS). Meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) task-based fMRI design with event-related runs; (I6) uses cognitive reappraisal (Increase/Decrease distancing/reinterpretation) as the regulation strategy; (I7) includes static visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) as an analyzed stimulus set (IAPS runs analyzed separately), even though the study also used film clips; (I8) sample is healthy adults and reported results for the healthy control sample (n=59); (I9) reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Increase>Look, Decrease>Look, Increase>Decrease) used in analyses; (I10) reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space (Tables and figures, FWE-corrected maps); (I11) whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. This full text meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using instructed reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect (I6) in response to static visual images from the IAPS (I7). This paper reports a task-based fMRI reappraisal study in healthy adults using static visual images (IAPS). The methods describe a reappraisal (Reapp Neg) versus view/look (Look Neg, Look Neu) task with anticipatory cues; the target sample is healthy adults (n=30 after exclusions). The analyses include within-task contrasts relating reappraisal (Reapp Neg–Look Neg) to outcomes and employ whole-brain voxelwise mediation and second-level robust regression; peak coordinates are reported in MNI space (e.g., left amygdala coordinates). Whole-brain thresholds and FWE correction are described and tables/figures present cluster results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study does not implement reappraisal (reinterpretation, perspective-taking, or distancing with an explicit regulation goal). Instead it uses an attentional distraction (bar-orientation) task to divert attention from stimuli, which is not reappraisal as defined by the review (I6 not met). Although this is a task-based fMRI study with static visual images and includes a healthy control group and within-task regulation contrasts (I5, I7, I8, I9 satisfied), the provided full text does not report whole-brain peak coordinates for group-level voxelwise maps in standard space (I10 not demonstrably met in the supplied content). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails to meet I6 (reappraisal strategy) and, based on the provided text, I10 (reported whole-brain peak coordinates).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly includes a reappraisal condition instructing participants to down-regulate their emotional response (meets I6). Emotional stimuli were static IAPS photographs (meets I7). The sample consists of screened healthy adults (ages 55–75) with exclusion of psychiatric/medical conditions (meets I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Reappraise > Observe; Reappraise vs. Label) (meets I9). Analyses were group-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise maps normalized to MNI space, and peak coordinates are reported throughout the results (meets I10 and I11). The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation (meets I5). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study meets several inclusion criteria (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: includes reappraisal as an emotion regulation strategy; I7: uses static visual images (IAPS pictures); I8: sample comprises healthy adults (HP and control groups with no history of psychiatric disorders); I9: reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraisal negative vs. view negative)). However, the fMRI analyses are described as ROI-based using anatomically defined masks from the WFU PickAtlas and ROI-specific FWE correction; the methods emphasize ROI analyses rather than a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level map. The reported activations appear to derive from ROI-restricted analyses (small-volume approach), and no whole-brain voxelwise, group-level statistical map with whole-brain peak coordinates and thresholds is reported. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI/SVC results without whole-brain maps) and fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I10 (group-level whole-brain coordinates). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal task (Suppress= reappraisal) with static visual images (IAPS). The sample includes a healthy control group reported separately. Relevant within-task contrasts are defined and reported (Maintain>Observe; Suppress>Maintain), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (with small-volume and whole-brain corrections) and peak coordinates are provided for seeds (MNI) and referred to Supplementary Tables for detailed whole-brain peaks. Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied: task-based fMRI, reappraisal strategy, static visual stimuli, healthy control group reported, within-task regulation contrasts, and group-level whole-brain maps with coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly implements cognitive reappraisal (instructions to reappraise) alongside suppression and appraisal, using static visual IAPS images (63 high-arousing negative pictures). The sample is healthy adults (N=42 females) screened for psychiatric/medical conditions. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to reappraisal (e.g., Target Reappraisal > Target Appraise; Target Reappraisal > Target Suppression) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected thresholds and MNI coordinates reported in tables/figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets I5–I11 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion while viewing static negative images (ERT). Participants were healthy adults with no psychiatric/neurological disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraisal vs. Maintain) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported (Table 1; MNI space described). The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis (task-based fMRI; reappraisal strategy; static visual stimuli; healthy adult sample; within-task regulation contrast; whole-brain coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria are met.

The paper reports a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs React) and includes a Faces task using Ekman face photographs (static visual images, albeit presented with a looming simulation). Healthy control (HC) participants are reported separately, with within-task group-level voxelwise contrasts (Reappraise > React) and whole-brain results given with peak coordinates in Talairach space. Thus the study satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal strategy), I7 (static visual stimuli for the Faces condition), I8 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation contrast), I10 (whole-brain group-level maps with coordinates), and I11 (results described in text/tables). Note: other tasks in the paper (video criticism, autobiographical beliefs) do not meet I7, but the Faces condition provides qualifying data for inclusion.

This article meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that implements cognitive reappraisal (reinterpretation/perspective-taking) to down-regulate responses to sad images (I6). The regulated stimuli are static visual images (IAPS and normed photographs) (I7). The paper includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (I8). The analyses report within-task regulation contrasts (reappraise-sad vs attend-sad / attend conditions) (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses were conducted with cluster-corrected thresholds and peak/localization information reported in tables (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or solely between-group-only reporting). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI task study of cognitive reappraisal (increase/decrease) in healthy adults with whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and reported peak coordinates; however, the regulation target during scanning was internally recalled memories of previously encoded images rather than static visual images presented during the task. The review’s stimulus inclusion criterion (I7) requires that the emotional stimuli being regulated are static visual images during the task; studies regulating imagined/recalled (internally generated) content do not qualify. Therefore, although criteria I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, and I11 are satisfied, criterion I7 is not met, so the study must be excluded.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) in which participants performed cognitive reappraisal (detach/experience) as the regulation strategy (I6). The regulated stimuli were static visual images from the IAPS (I7). The sample includes healthy adult participants (younger and older groups) with exclusion criteria applied and separate reporting (I8). The manuscript reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Positive-Regulate > Positive-Experience; Negative-Regulate > Negative-Experience) (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, cluster-corrected, and peak coordinates are reported in MNI space with tables/figures (I10, I11). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided and complete. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study using reappraisal of static visual images (I5, I6, I7 met). It includes a healthy control group (I8 met) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with peak coordinates (I10, I11 met). However, the paper does not report within-task whole-brain activation contrasts for the healthy control group alone (e.g., HC: Reappraise > Baseline); instead it reports (a) main effects across all participants and (b) between-group contrasts (HC vs anxious). The meta-analysis requires at least one within-task contrast for the healthy control sample itself. Because that inclusion criterion (I9) is not satisfied, the study is ineligible for inclusion. No exclusion criteria from the list (E4–E8) are otherwise triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed cognitive reappraisal paradigm (downregulation and upregulation) with static visual images (IAPS). Participants were healthy adult students screened for medical/psychiatric history. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., downregulate vs negative look, upregulate vs negative look) and performs whole-brain voxelwise RFX analyses with cluster correction; Talairach coordinates for peak activations are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of criteria. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the stimulus criterion required by the review. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal/perspective-taking strategy used), I8 (healthy adult sample reported), and I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered by the provided text. Full text appears complete for core sections (intro, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is excluded because the emotional stimuli regulated during the fMRI task are outcomes of a social decision-making task (Ultimatum Game offers and proposers' faces/intentions), not static visual images. Inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli = static visual images such as IAPS pictures or photographs) is not met: although the authors trained participants on reappraisal using static IAPS pictures, the scanned regulation task targeted emotions elicited by monetary offers/proposer intentions (social decision outcomes), which are explicitly excluded by I7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal strategy used), I8 (healthy adult sample), and I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts). I10 (reporting whole-brain peak coordinates) is unclear in the provided excerpt and thus not assumed met. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion).

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants that explicitly implemented cognitive reappraisal as an emotion-regulation strategy and compared reappraisal vs control (e.g., RU vs CUR contrasts). Emotional stimuli were static visual images (IAPS pictures). The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) and provides peak coordinates (MNI converted to Talairach) and tables/figures of activations. All inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied (task-based fMRI; reappraisal strategy; static visual stimuli; healthy adult sample; within-task regulation contrasts reported; whole-brain group-level maps with coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion requirements for the review: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that implements cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion (I6) using static visual stimuli (IAPS photographs; I7). The sample is a healthy adult community cohort with screening for psychiatric disorders and separate reporting for the healthy group (I8). The key within-task contrast for regulation (regulate negative > look negative) is reported (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space and whole-brain correction for the regulate>look contrast (I10), and results/coordinates are clearly described in text/figures (I11). Full text contains background, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using static visual stimuli (faces) (I7) and it includes a healthy control group (I8). However it does NOT use reappraisal (no reinterpretation/distancing/up-/down-regulation instructions); the task is an implicit emotional-interference (attend/ignore) paradigm, so I6 is not met. The paper does not report any within-task reappraisal-related contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) for the healthy group, so I9 is not met. Analyses appear focused on a priori ROIs (and an exploratory ROI mask) without reporting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map with comprehensive peak coordinates (I10 not met). Exclusion criterion E5 applies (ROI-only reporting without an accompanying whole-brain map). Hence the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly implemented reappraisal as an emotion-regulation strategy (Sad-Reappraise condition) using static visual images (sad photographs). The sample are adult females screened to exclude current mood, anxiety, or substance disorders (no MDD), so a healthy adult sample is available. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., Sad-Reappraise > Sad-View) and describes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects/FILM) with normalization to MNI space and tabulated cluster results (Z values and referenced tables), consistent with reporting of peak coordinates in standard space. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I11.

The study meets many inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI; use of reappraisal as a regulation strategy; static visual stimuli [IAPS images]; includes a healthy control group with separate within-group and between-group contrasts; reports within-task regulation contrasts such as reappraisal vs. view). However, the fMRI analyses were conducted using anatomically defined ROI masks (AAL-based) to examine the amygdala and regulation networks, and the manuscript frames results in terms of these ROIs. There is no clear evidence of an accompanying whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation map or comprehensive whole-brain coordinate table independent of ROI-restricted results. Therefore the study appears to report only ROI-focused analyses and not whole-brain results, violating inclusion criterion I10 and meeting exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only/small-volume-corrected results without whole-brain map). Full text appears complete.

The full text lacks a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map with peak coordinates for a reappraisal (regulation) contrast (I10 not met). The study reports task-based fMRI (I5) using reappraisal (I6) of static visual images (I7) in a healthy control sample reported separately (I8), and it presents within-task regulation contrasts (Look vs Decrease) via ROI analyses (I9). However, primary activation results are ROI-based (amygdala) and the reported coordinates pertain to PPI connectivity restricted to IFG, not a whole-brain activation map. This meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only / no whole-brain map). Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study (N=58 healthy adults) that implemented instruction-induced reappraisal to down-regulate emotional responses to static visual images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Reappraise > Attend, Attend > Reappraise, Instruction × Valence) at the group level. Whole-brain random-effects analyses were conducted (reported thresholding and whole-brain results) and peak coordinates are provided in MNI space for key activations (DLPFC, OFC, amygdala). The sample consists of healthy adults with exclusions for psychiatric/neurological disorders, and behavioral and imaging results are reported separately for this group. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, clinical-only samples, or non-empirical article) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) task-based fMRI; (I6) used cognitive reappraisal (decrease instruction; training included reinterpretation/perspective strategies); (I7) stimuli were static visual images (IAPS and child image set); (I8) sample includes healthy young adults (ages 18–22) within the reported sample of healthy participants; (I9) reports within-task regulation contrast (decrease negative > look negative); (I10) reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (Talairach coordinates in tables); (I11) whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures/supplementary material. No exclusion criteria apply (none of E4–E8 are met). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and coordinate tables referenced). Thus the study is eligible for inclusion in the adult reappraisal whole-brain coordinate meta-analysis, noting that reported contrasts are from a mixed-age sample rather than adult-only analyses.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly includes a cognitive reappraisal condition (REAP) employing reinterpretation/’pretend unreal’ instructions. Stimuli were static visual images (IAPS and photos), and the sample comprises healthy adult volunteers (N=19, no neurological/psychiatric history). The paper reports within-task contrasts and condition-specific analyses (e.g., social pleasant vs nonsocial pleasant and social unpleasant vs nonsocial unpleasant) across viewing conditions including REAP, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and peak coordinates reported (MNI) and thresholding described. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults using distancing (reappraisal) and reports whole-brain group-level coordinates and regulation contrasts; however, the regulated stimuli are monetary reward anticipation cues (coin cues) rather than static emotional images. This violates inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be static visual images such as IAPS pictures/faces/scenes; anticipatory cues are explicitly excluded). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I7. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) directly apply.

Excluded because inclusion criterion I7 is not met: the regulated stimuli are anticipatory threat/pain cues and occasional electric shocks (instructed fear/anticipatory anxiety), not static visual images. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (reappraisal used — distancing), I8 (healthy adult sample reported), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported, e.g., R–NR), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI reported), and I11 (coordinates/tables described). No exclusion criteria from E4–E8 apply. Therefore the study does not match the review’s required stimulus type (I7) and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using static visual stimuli (paintings and names) and reports whole-brain results with coordinates. However, it does NOT implement an explicit reappraisal emotion-regulation task or instructions (participants made preference choices; the paper interprets processes as “reappraisal-like” but does not instruct reinterpretation/perspective-taking/distancing as a regulation strategy), nor does it report within-task contrasts explicitly comparing reappraisal vs. baseline (e.g., “reappraise > look”) related to emotion regulation. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I6 (reappraisal used as the emotion regulation strategy) and I9 (reports at least one within-task emotion-regulation contrast). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]). Full text appears complete.

The full text describes an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=30) that used reappraisal (reinterpretation/distancing) to downregulate emotion to static visual images (IAPS). Group-level within-task contrasts related to reappraisal (e.g., reappraisal emotional vs. view emotional) are reported, and whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and tables of activation peaks are described (standard MNI space). The methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI with explicit reappraisal instruction (REAP “pretend unreal”), using static visual images (IAPS and other photographs), healthy adult sample (19 healthy women), reports within-task regulation contrasts (REAP vs NAT, REAP vs ESUP), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space (tables/figures). Full text contains methods, results, and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of reappraisal effects on static visual stimuli with whole-brain coordinates.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) task-based fMRI with BOLD acquisition and analysis; (I6) uses cognitive reappraisal (distancing/reinterpretation) as the regulation strategy; (I7) stimuli are static visual images from IAPS (photographs/scenes); (I8) participants are healthy adults (younger and older) screened for neurological/psychiatric disorders and MMSE reported; (I9) reports within-task contrasts relating to regulation (Reappraise > Experience and Experience > Reappraise); (I10) presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (z-thresholds, cluster correction) and reports peak coordinates in MNI space in tables; (I11) whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that used a cognitive reappraisal paradigm (reinterpretation/distancing instructions: INCREASE, DECREASE, MAINTAIN) with static visual stimuli (IAPS and supplemented pictures). The sample includes a healthy control group of adults reported separately; within-group contrasts and behavioral ratings are reported for controls. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (DECREASE > MAINTAIN, INCREASE > MAINTAIN) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space presented in tables (and figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not empathy-without-regulation, and provides whole-brain maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the review.

Although this task-based fMRI paper meets most methodological requirements (uses static visual stimuli [faces], reports within-task regulation-related contrasts, includes a healthy control group with results reported separately, and provides whole-brain group analyses with cluster coordinates), it does not use reappraisal as the emotion-regulation strategy (I6). The study employs affect labeling (verbal labeling of facial affect), described as incidental emotion regulation, which is conceptually distinct from cognitive reappraisal strategies such as reinterpretation, perspective-taking, or distancing specified in the inclusion criteria. Because I6 (reappraisal strategy) is not satisfied, the study does not qualify for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) apply based on the provided full text.

This is a task-based fMRI study of elderly GAD vs. non-anxious controls using a personalized worry-induction/suppression paradigm delivered as written sentences and instructed mental imagery/recall. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (healthy control group reported separately), I9 (within-task contrasts: WI–RS and WS–RS), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (regulation strategy is worry suppression/induction using scripts and mental imagery — not reappraisal/reinterpretation/perspective-taking aimed at changing appraisal), I7 (stimuli are personalized sentences and imagined memories, not static visual images). No exclusion criteria from the review (E4–E8) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not implement reappraisal nor regulate static visual images (fails I6 and I7).

This fMRI study used a task (I5) in which participants were trained to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion (I6). The regulated stimuli were static IAPS images (I7). The sample included a healthy control group with no history of anxiety or mood disorders (NA group), satisfying the requirement for a healthy adult group (I8). The report includes within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reduce vs. Maintain; I9) and describes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with images normalized to Talairach space and significant clusters reported in Tables (I10). The manuscript presents whole-brain results in text/figures/tables (I11). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) are met based on the provided full text. Confidence is slightly reduced because the excerpt does not reproduce the numeric peak coordinates explicitly, but the methods and referenced tables/figures indicate that whole-brain peak coordinates were reported.

This is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adult participants that explicitly implemented cognitive reappraisal (down-regulation) during viewing of static visual images (IAPS and in-house pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., reappraise > view, reappraise > suppress, view > reappraise) and presents whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates referenced to standard space (MNI). This full text meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that uses cognitive reappraisal (increase/decrease/maintain) as the regulation strategy (I6) while participants view static visual images from the IAPS (I7). The sample consists of healthy adults with exclusion of psychiatric/neurological disorders (I8). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based BOLD fMRI study (I5) that implements reappraisal via a distancing strategy to down-regulate negative emotion (I6). Full text presents a task-based fMRI experiment using instructed reappraisal (reinterpretation) of negative IAPS pictures (static visual stimuli). While this is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using static visual stimuli (partner facial photographs) (I7), with a healthy adult sample reported separately (I8), and whole-brain group-level results with peak coordinates reported (I10) and acceptable reporting (I11), it does NOT implement an explicit reappraisal or instructed emotion-regulation manipulation. This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly implemented cognitive reappraisal (instruction to “decrease” via reinterpretation) using static visual images (IAPS and matched photographs). This is an fMRI task study with healthy control group and whole-brain coordinates reported (meets I5, I8, I10). However it does NOT test reappraisal or any explicit emotion-regulation instruction (violates I6), the regulated stimuli are auditory script-driven imagery (narrative/imagined scenarios) not static visual images (violates I7), and it provides no within-task reappraisal/regulation contrast such as “reappraise > look” (violates I9). This study is a task-based fMRI experiment that uses an explicit reappraisal instruction (ignore emotional expression and rate attractiveness) to down-regulate emotional responses to static visual images (photographs of faces). Participants were healthy adults and group-level within-task contrasts comparing high-control (reappraise) to low-control (rate) are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion provided.

The study is task-based fMRI using cognitive reappraisal (I5, I6). It includes a healthy control group reported separately (I8), reports within-task regulation contrasts (reappraise vs react) (I9), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with Talairach coordinates (I10). However, the regulated stimuli are autobiographical scripts and flashed negative self-belief text (sentence-based/narrative), not static visual images (e.g., IAPS pictures or photographs). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I7 (static visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the regulated stimuli were recalled autobiographical memories cued by phrases (internally generated/imagined), not static visual images; this fails inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be static visual images). The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (used reappraisal-like strategies: analyze = reinterpretation, accept = distancing), I8 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), and I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with Talairach coordinates). This study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults using static face stimuli and reports whole-brain coordinates (meets I5, I7, I8, I10, I11). The sample consists of healthy young adults screened for neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease negative > look negative and its inverse) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation results with peak coordinates reported in tables/figures (SPM2 normalized coordinates). Full article text (methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adults that uses cognitive reappraisal and reports whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts with Talairach coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be static images) and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of reappraisal using static IAPS images in healthy adult volunteers (satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8). However, the full text presents primarily seed-based PPI (psychophysiological interaction) connectivity analyses and does not report a group-level whole-brain, task-evoked activation contrast for emotion regulation (e.g., Reappraise > Maintain) with peak coordinates that would qualify as the target activation map. Although an amygdala conjunction was used to define the seed, the paper’s main results are connectivity-based and no standard whole-brain activation contrast table/peaks for the regulation contrast are provided in this article (I9 and I10 not met). Therefore the study effectively reports only seed-based connectivity without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map, meeting exclusion criterion E6. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly implemented cognitive reappraisal (increase/decrease) during viewing of static visual images (IAPS). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease > attend) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak Talairach coordinates and cluster results; a healthy control group is included and reported separately. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that trained a ‘cognitive control’ (reality checking) strategy and reports group-level whole-brain coordinates (Talairach) for relevant contrasts (I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, I11 satisfied). However, the regulation was applied during the anticipation/expectation period (participants performed reality checking while awaiting pictures) rather than during regulation of the actual static visual stimuli themselves. The review’s I7 requires that the emotional stimuli being regulated are static visual images (e.g., IAPS pictures); it explicitly excludes studies in which the regulated stimuli are anticipatory cues. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I7 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E4–E8) were triggered by the report.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study that trained participants to use cognitive reappraisal strategies (increase/decrease) to regulate responses to negative IAPS images. Stimuli were static visual images. Sample consists of healthy adults (ages 61–65) with no reported neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports within-task contrasts (increase vs attend; decrease vs attend) and a voxelwise whole-brain ANOVA with results transformed to Talairach space and reported as clusters/coordinates. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This full text meets all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly uses reappraisal strategies (increase, decrease, distancing) as the regulation manipulation (I6). The regulated stimuli are static visual IAPS pictures (threat-related) (I7). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (24 right-handed female volunteers) with no reported disorders (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (increase > view, decrease > view, view > decrease) for the target sample (I9). Group-level whole-brain analyses are performed and peak coordinates are reported in MNI space (tables/figures report coordinates) (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), the study is empirical, reports task activations rather than only connectivity, and reports within-subject task contrasts for healthy controls. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).
